races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with three C&D wins who thrives in sprint finishes but carries 7lb penalty from recent Wolverhampton success
runners_data.comment: Three wins over C&D and still 1lb below his last winning mark; capable of playing a part
runners_data.spotlight: Three C&D wins but perhaps even more effective on Tapeta; had the benefit of Jack Callan's claim when successful at Wolverhampton (7f) last month and although back up 3lb he's perfectly capable of finding another race off this mark.

runners_data.name: Yehudi
runners_data.note: Prominent racer better suited to Polytrack surfaces with strong recent 7f form and 29-day freshness break
runners_data.comment: 3lb lower than when beaten a neck over C&D in February; continued in form since; player
runners_data.spotlight: Has done most of his AW racing on Wolverhampton Tapeta but he's run his two best races on Kempton Polytrack (7f), going close in February and breaking his duck last month; back up 4lb; a likely contender on course debut.

runners_data.name: Francisco
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two 7f AW wins including C&D victory who disappointed on turf but returns to preferred surface
runners_data.comment: Yet to score on turf but last month he recorded his second AW win, at this track (7f).
runners_data.spotlight: Two 7f handicap wins on the AW, the latest over C&D in April under Charlie Tucker, but he was disappointing on the turf track here (7f) since, given that he's handled that test in the past; shade to prove this time.

runners_data.name: Enpassant
runners_data.note: Late closer with three 7f AW wins elsewhere who struggled on quick turf return but better suited back on Polytrack
runners_data.comment: Won at Southwell but beat only 2 home there turned out 8 days later; needs to bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Three 7f wins on AW elsewhere, most recently at Southwell in April; a quick return didn't pay off there next time and he was always behind when returned to turf at Leicester last month; has run well over C&D in the past, though, so he may be more himself this time.

runners_data.name: Fort Augustus
runners_data.note: Strong late finisher with two wins from last three at Southwell, headgear fitted, and proven quick turnaround ability
runners_data.comment: Didn't look to have any excuses as favourite over C&D latest but this weaker if anything
runners_data.spotlight: Won two of last three at Southwell (7f) since these aids were fitted, a steady late surge taking him to the front close home 14 days ago; acts on Polytrack, too, but plenty needs to go right today from a wide draw.

runners_data.name: Majestic Wave
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse down 24lb in weights after poor recent form but yard debut here showed promise over 6f
runners_data.comment: Winless for his current yard and he ended last term under a cloud; big step forward needed
runners_data.spotlight: Won 6f maiden at Navan as 2yo; promising yard debut over 6f on this track in February 2025 but he's mostly struggled since, thus the drop of 24lb in the weights since racing in Britain; should come on for his April reappearance and is one to keep an eye on for signs of a revival.

runners_data.name: Dashing Donkey
runners_data.note: Front-runner with four turf wins but 0-9 AW record creates major surface concerns despite tactical advantages
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins from the front on turf, over 7f in 2024 and twice over 1m at Newmarket last summer; 0-9 on AW but he handles this surface and is not a forlorn hope on the return to 7f.

runners_data.name: Secret Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with three wins this year including C&D but last three runs well below previous standards
runners_data.comment: Well behind a couple of these over C&D a month ago; needs more from somewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Won at 6f and over C&D for James Owen at the start of the year, then over 1m here on yard debut in March, but his last three runs have been nothing like as good; has plenty to prove back at 7f.

runners_data.name: Adelaide Bay
runners_data.note: Late closer with three 7f Polytrack/Tapeta wins between April-June but out of luck since November for different trainers
runners_data.comment: Maybe the return to this yard, for whom he won three times last season, will do the trick
runners_data.spotlight: Three 7f wins on Polytrack and Tapeta between April and June in 2025 for this yard; right out of luck for different trainers from November onwards but he fell a long way in the weights and shot home to take a late second at Southwell (7f) 14 days ago; should make hay off current mark, 6lb lower than latest win, if overcoming a wide draw.

runners_data.name: Oberon Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Newcastle Tapeta ability but 78-day layoff and poor recent Kempton form raise fitness doubts
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of ability over 7f on Newcastle Tapeta but failed to stay 1m on handicap debut at Wetherby in April 2025; wasn't seen again until well beaten on Kempton AW (6f) in March for new yard, where he bled from the nose; best watched for now.

runners_data.name: Twitch
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who often leads but couldn't maintain position on turf recently and faces competitive field despite low weight
runners_data.comment: Without a win since 2024 but went close here last month; not dismissed.
runners_data.spotlight: Often leads; tight between him and Francisco on C&D form in April but he couldn't hold his place on the turf track here since and this looks competitive, especially with others in the field who like to lead.

runners_data.name: Harbour Vision
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader with tremendous AW record but fading pattern in recent starts and 55-day break raise stamina concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Tremendous win record on AW, successful 16 times; however, the last 11 have been at Wolverhampton and he's gone off the boil since winning two in a row there (7f) at the start of the year; has it to prove in first Polytrack run for over a year.

races.paceDynamic: Harbour Vision is the sole confirmed front runner but comes with major stamina concerns after fading badly in recent outings. With minimal early pressure from Yehudi, Dashing Donkey and Twitch sitting prominent, Harbour Vision should be allowed comfortable sectionals through the early stages before the field closes up entering the final 2f. The weak pace setup will compress the field and create a sprint finish where positioning and a turn of foot matter more than sustained stamina. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with tactical speed who can weave through traffic and quicken when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harbour Vision Fades Early
scenarios.trigger: If Harbour Vision's stamina gives out before the 2f pole as recent form suggests
scenarios.body: The pace collapses completely and turns into a tactical crawl, allowing the classiest hold-up horses with the best turn of foot to dominate the finish. Split Elevens and Fort Augustus benefit most from the stop-start nature and sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi or Dashing Donkey pressure Harbour Vision from the 4f marker
scenarios.body: The tempo lifts significantly in the middle stages, stretching the field and creating a more honest gallop that plays to horses with proven stamina at the trip. Francisco and Enpassant's proven 7f form comes to the fore in a more searching test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Harbour Vision Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Harbour Vision's 55-day break has refreshed his stamina and he kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: The field gets strung out chasing the leader's sustained effort, creating gaps and allowing patient hold-up horses to pick their way through. Fort Augustus and Adelaide Bay can time their runs to perfection in the spaces created.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Takeover
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi or Twitch take over from a fading Harbour Vision and maintain strong gallop
scenarios.body: The race develops into a front-running battle where the prominent racers who inherit the lead can dictate terms to the closers. Dashing Donkey's front-running ability becomes crucial despite his poor AW record.

watchPoints.text: Harbour Vision's stamina management - if he fades before the 2f pole the pace will collapse into a tactical crawl
Traffic problems for hold-up horses Split Elevens and Fort Augustus if the pace stays strong and field remains bunched
Yehudi's surface switching from preferred Tapeta to Polytrack and whether Billy Loughnane can position him prominently
Francisco and Adelaide Bay both returning to AW after poor turf runs - watch for immediate improvement back on preferred surface
Weight differential impact with Twitch getting 17lb from top-weighted Majestic Wave in what could become a sprint finish

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap

runners_data.name: Peregrine Falcon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been competitive in tight finishes over 5f but remains a maiden after 14 attempts
runners_data.comment: Had 13 cracks at it now; while she's consistent, she's fully exposed; returns from a break
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden after 14 runs, five under Billy Loughnane, but has been involved in tight finishes over 5f on Tapeta on three occasions so ought to find a race at some stage and perhaps this first go on Polytrack will suit.

runners_data.name: Shalaa Asker
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three 5f wins whose style suits this pace setup despite a flat recent run at Southwell
runners_data.comment: Drawn wide on turf last time; usually gives his running here, so holds each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: Busy since the autumn; some narrow defeats to go with three 5f wins, on Polytrack elsewhere and Tapeta; ran flat at Southwell recently but he's realistically weighted if that wasn't a sign that he's going off the boil.

runners_data.name: Balon d'Or
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning fresh after 45 days with a significant 9lb weight drop since November
runners_data.spotlight: Both handicap wins on turf at Chester (5f and 6f); no great shakes on this track for new yard since November but he's dropped 9lb in that time and there was the glimmer of a revival here last time when back from a break; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent poor form suggests he may struggle to sustain his early position
runners_data.comment: 0-5 on turf; flopped on AW last time and others hold more pressing claims
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden; two poor efforts of late, with and without a hood, but he ran well for a long way behind a subsequent winner at Wolverhampton (6f) in April and is worth another go at 5f; first-time blinkers today.

runners_data.name: Diamond Dreamer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and course winner who finished fast when runner-up here in March at this exact distance
runners_data.comment: More prolific on AW than turf; solid third at Lingfield two weeks ago; each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner who came close to ending a losing AW run when a fast-closing runner-up here (5f) in March (5f); returns to this C&D for the first time since and ought to go well if the race falls his way.

runners_data.name: Desdemona
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two recent wins who overcame a wide draw when successful at this course and distance
runners_data.comment: Has won over C&D, and also earlier this year on the AW tracks here and at Chelmsford.
runners_data.spotlight: Tough filly who took time to find her form again but won two in a row in early spring, over C&D (overcame a wide draw) and at Chelmsford (5f), and subsequent defeats came over 6f then very slowly away here in April; form claims.

runners_data.name: Honour Your Dreams
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who benefits from a 7lb weight allowance but has never won in 22 AW attempts
runners_data.spotlight: Six turf wins, three in 2025; 0-22 on AW and although having a healthy pull at the weights with Desdemona on their C&D run in February he's not looked in peak form on last two starts.

races.paceDynamic: Style King and Honour Your Dreams will take this along early from their prominent positions, with Peregrine Falcon likely tracking just behind the leaders. The pace should be sustainable rather than frantic given the limited speed in this field, allowing the hold-up horses Shalaa Asker, Diamond Dreamer, Desdemona and Balon d'Or to position themselves for late challenges. With the majority of the field preferring to come from off the pace and Style King's recent poor form suggesting he may not sustain his effort, this race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can time their runs from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Style King and Honour Your Dreams set a moderate pace that suits closers...
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop allows Shalaa Asker, Diamond Dreamer and Desdemona to unleash powerful finishing kicks in the final furlong. The front-runners fade as the closers sweep past with superior finishing speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners prosper
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slower than expected and front-runners can conserve energy...
scenarios.body: Peregrine Falcon gets first run on the leaders while Honour Your Dreams benefits from his weight allowance to stay on strongly. The hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by the lack of pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Course specialist strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Dreamer reproduces her fast-closing March run at this course and distance...
scenarios.body: Her proven ability to finish strongly here gives her the edge over rivals less suited to the track characteristics. The pace sets up perfectly for her trademark late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider benefits from chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish from the turn...
scenarios.body: Balon d'Or's drop in weight and freshness from a 45-day break allows him to capitalise on a messy finish. The lack of early pace neutralises the usual hold-up advantage.

watchPoints.text: Style King may stop quickly if pressured early given his recent poor form and inability to sustain effort
Diamond Dreamer's finishing kick could be devastating if she reproduces her fast-closing March effort here
Honour Your Dreams needs to translate his turf form to AW having failed in all 22 previous all-weather attempts
Shalaa Asker showed flat form last time at Southwell which could indicate a dip in current condition
The sustainable early pace will likely favour the five hold-up horses over the two prominent runners

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 'Confined' EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (2 Runs Or Less) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Sunshine Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong pedigree connections but must bounce back from disappointing Sandown effort 41 days ago
runners_data.comment: Just beaten on Kempton debut last autumn but disappointing on return; worth another chance
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to connections' Oaks winner Soul Sister; close second to useful rival at Kempton (1m, AW) on sole 2yo start; managed only sixth when odds-on favourite for good Sandown novice (1m2f, good) in April but this race looks much easier and the return to Polytrack will suit; good chance.

runners_data.name: Kashooda
runners_data.note: Debut runner from powerful Balding yard with sister who won at this level in France
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth foal; sister to French 7f 2yo/9.7f winner Khadidja, half-sister to three winners including Kawida (7f/1m 2yo including Listed; RPR 106) and Khinjani (1m2f; 94); dam 9.4f winner (68), half-sister to Australian 1m1f/1m2f Group 1 winner Zaaki; in good hands; market may guide on debut.

runners_data.name: Northern Bea
runners_data.note: First-timer with excellent pedigree but trainer struggling for winners this season
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000gns yearling; eighth foal; closely related to 1m4f winner Royal Associate (RPR 99), half-sister to three winners including Kingfisher King (1m2f; 106) and Officer Of State (1m7f; 103); dam unplaced 1m-1m2f in France; makes debut in a race lacking strength in depth.

runners_data.name: Lightning Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who should get uncontested lead and has recent course form
runners_data.comment: Fourth on her Kempton debut three weeks ago, finishing just over 3l behind Royal Fanfare
runners_data.spotlight: Fair form when making the frame on both starts this spring, more recently when third of 11 at Southwell (1m); holds each-way claims at least if suited by the longer trip here.

runners_data.name: Antiquarian
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was flattered by slow pace at Ascot and faces traffic concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled on 2yo debut (6f) and was almost certainly flattered by proximity to principals when sixth of seven in slowly run contest at Ascot (1m2f, good) last month.

runners_data.name: Shopaholic
runners_data.note: Older filly carrying penalty whose best form came over course and distance in April
runners_data.comment: May do better but is unlikely to reverse Lingfield placings with Knights Charge
runners_data.spotlight: Made fairly encouraging debut when fifth of eight over C&D in April and may not have been suited by good to soft turf when below that form last month but others in this line-up look stronger.

runners_data.name: Arrivera
runners_data.note: Long absence of 154 days since moderate debut effort suggests significant issues
runners_data.spotlight: First foal from a useful 7f AW winner; showed only a glimmer of promise before weakening into sixth of seven on debut at Southwell (1m) on New Year's Day.

runners_data.name: Coral Cathedral
runners_data.note: Juvenile who showed inexperience on debut and likely needs more time to develop
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a German Group 3 winner; too green to do herself justice when 33-1 for debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in December; needs to have made good progress in the meantime.

runners_data.name: Musical Accord
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from in-form Beckett stable but has yet to show winning form
runners_data.spotlight: Midfield in fairly good Newbury maiden (1m2f, good) on debut in April but unable to land any sort of blow at Wolverhampton (9.4f) last month; needs to up her game here.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: Weak debut form at long odds suggests limited ability despite decent breeding
runners_data.comment: Makes some appeal on pedigree and the market should indicate what is expected
runners_data.spotlight: Has a good pedigree but was always behind when 100-1 for recent debut at Southwell (1m).

runners_data.name: Kenkelly
runners_data.note: Lightly raced type who was well beaten in small field at Yarmouth despite prominent position
runners_data.comment: Modest third at Yarmouth but may do better with the outing under her belt
runners_data.spotlight: Probably didn't achieve a great deal when well-held third of five in race won easily by short-odds favourite at Yarmouth (11.5f, good to firm) in April and was soundly beaten when dropped to 1m2f at Goodwood last month.

runners_data.name: Hunting Berries
runners_data.note: Completely out of her depth based on two poor efforts at shorter distances
runners_data.comment: 150-1 when a well-beaten last of 12 on her debut over 6f here last September
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at triple-digit odds on first two starts (6f/1m); upped in trip again here.

runners_data.name: Corallience
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was well beaten behind Sunshine Star at Sandown six weeks ago
runners_data.comment: Bottom of this pack judged on her 2yo effort at Newbury
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced on 2yo debut at Newbury (1m, soft) but suffered heavy defeat when reappearing at Sandown (1m2f, good; behind Sunshine Star) six weeks ago.

races.paceDynamic: Lightning Glory will take this field along at a sustainable pace with no obvious challenger for the early lead. With most rivals adopting hold-up tactics (Antiquarian, Musical Accord, Coral Cathedral, Blue Tulip, Hunting Berries, Corallience), the gallop will likely be modest through the early stages before quickening significantly from the home turn. Sunshine Star represents the main prominent threat to press Lightning Glory, but her style suggests tracking rather than disputing. This tactical setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems behind and capitalize on the solid pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lightning Glory Leads Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lightning Glory gets an uncontested lead and the pace stays reasonable
scenarios.body: The confirmed front-runner will dictate terms and prove difficult to peg back when the field fans out late. Her recent third at Southwell shows she stays this trip and can handle the tactical pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sunshine Star Class Tells
scenarios.trigger: If the well-bred filly can overcome her Sandown disappointment and travel into contention
scenarios.body: Her connections' record with fillies and half-sister's Oaks success suggests significant untapped ability that could emerge. William Buick's presence adds tactical nous to capitalize on any pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Lightning Glory goes too slowly early and the race becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The large contingent of hold-up horses including Musical Accord and Corallience could benefit from a muddling pace. However, traffic problems in a 13-runner field make this scenario fraught with danger.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If either Kashooda or Northern Bea shows significant improvement from their respective yards
scenarios.body: Both debutants have strong pedigrees and connections capable of producing ready-made performers. Their unknown quantities could exploit any tactical naivety from the experienced runners.

watchPoints.text: Lightning Glory must be monitored for any early pressure as her front-running tactics become crucial if challenged
Watch for market support for debutants Kashooda and Northern Bea as their yards rarely run unprepared horses
Sunshine Star's early positioning will be critical given her prominent style in a race lacking early pace
Traffic problems likely in home straight with so many hold-up horses requiring clear runs
Any significant drift in Lightning Glory's odds could signal connections expect stronger pace pressure

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaori
runners_data.note: Returns after 255 days off but showed consistent form as a 2yo and gets prominent position behind likely soft pace
runners_data.spotlight: Made the frame on all three 2yo starts, most notably when third of 12 in Leicester maiden (7f, good to soft) in September; makes handicap/AW debut after 255-day absence but has plenty of scope for improvement in middle-distance handicaps this year.

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been crying out for this longer trip after three solid efforts over 1m this year
runners_data.spotlight: Three good runs over 1m this year, the latest in refitted blinkers at Kempton four weeks ago, but probably needs this longer trip to unlock some improvement.

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Front-runner with excellent recent record for new stable and will get dream scenario with uncontested lead
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner with 3-6 strike-rate for new stable this year, the latest win gained in four-runner contest at Wolverhampton (9.4f) last month; enjoyed the run of the race that day and has gone up another 6lb but is evidently in excellent nick.

runners_data.name: Extraterrestrial
runners_data.note: Raced too freely on turf last time but has shown good AW form and gets prominent pitch with William Buick aboard
runners_data.spotlight: Well down the field after racing too freely on turf last month but was in good form beforehand, most notably when close second at Southwell (1m3f; first-time cheekpieces) two runs ago; in the mix if back on song.

runners_data.name: Raspoutine
runners_data.note: Won here in April and has maintained form since, perfectly suited to track the leader in this small field
runners_data.spotlight: Won in good style here (1m) on seasonal/handicap debut in April and made the frame on both starts since, more recently when upped to 1m2f at Salisbury 12 days ago; returns to this track with first-time blinkers fitted; may still have more improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Central Command
runners_data.note: Must bounce back from poor turf run but showed his AW ability with emphatic Newcastle win last time out
runners_data.comment: Up 7lb for this turf debut but there was plenty to like about his Newcastle win (1m2f, AW)
runners_data.spotlight: Needs to bounce back quickly from very disappointing turf debut at Haydock a fortnight ago but came from off the pace for emphatic win at Newcastle (1m2f) on seasonal/handicap debut in early May, and has obvious claims if judged on that performance.

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Express will dictate terms from the front as the sole confirmed early leader, likely to get an uncontested lead through comfortable fractions. The prominent racers Kaori, Extraterrestrial, and Raspoutine will settle in behind but none are aggressive pace pressers, while hold-up horses Booziebrunch and Central Command will be anchored at the rear. With minimal pace pressure on the leader, this sets up as a tactical affair where front-runners and those able to track the pace closely will hold significant advantages. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close to the pace without having to make ground from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express gets soft fractions and stays the trip
scenarios.body: The front-runner will have too much in reserve when challenged, capitalizing on his tactical advantage and recent winning form. His ability to control the race tempo without pressure will prove decisive in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to find out the leader
scenarios.body: Raspoutine or Kaori will be perfectly positioned to strike in the final furlong, benefiting from a strong pace without being caught up in it. The winner will have tracked the leader closely before quickening when it matters most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Central Command or Booziebrunch will have the most untapped energy for a sustained finish, turning their poor position into an asset. The slow pace will allow closers to make up significant ground in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Distance Specialist Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the trip truly tests stamina reserves of pace horses
scenarios.body: Booziebrunch will benefit most from the step up to 1m2f, finally finding the distance that unlocks his potential. His recent good form over shorter trips suggests he has ability waiting to be unleashed at this longer distance.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Extraterrestrial settles better than last time as his free-running cost him dear at Haydock
Watch for any market moves on Kaori given the 255-day absence and step into handicap company
Watch the early pace as Lexington Express may get softer fractions than ideal for his finishing kick
Watch if Central Command can recapture his Newcastle form after disappointing turf debut
Watch how Booziebrunch handles the step up in trip as this could unlock significant improvement

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Diamondinthedark
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 187-day break faces fitness concerns despite impressive debut win
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark on her second start, at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in November; steps up in trip on handicap debut on first run since and may well show improvement; market will be best guide.

runners_data.name: Doodling
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent form who should benefit from the anticipated strong early pace
runners_data.comment: Could improve now handicapping but she will need to if she is to defy this opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 but was only beaten a neck on her second start/AW debut at Kempton (1m) in April; two lesser runs since, including on handicap debut when eighth of 14 at Salisbury (7f, good) 12 days ago; first-time cheekpieces need to have the desired effect.

runners_data.name: Polka Blue
runners_data.note: Recent Leicester winner whose prominent style suits but faces tougher opposition stepping up in class
runners_data.comment: 0-6 but she has shown promise, including on her handicap debut; now drops back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Following a series of near misses, she got her head in front when it mattered, down in trip and back on turf at Leicester (6f, good to firm) nine days ago; equally effective at 7f; strong claims under 6lb penalty in follow-up bid.

runners_data.name: Sahana
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner whose hold-up style perfectly matches the expected race shape
runners_data.comment: Off six months, albeit she defied a similar absence last season; no hood today
runners_data.spotlight: Opened her account when scoring over C&D in September; ran up to that form on her appearance when runner-up at Kempton (7f, AW) last month, without her regular hood (also absent here); looks sure to make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: Pretty Danielle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs the pace to collapse to be competitive from this mark
runners_data.comment: 0-7 but she returned after a break with a close third at Lingfield (7f, AW); respected
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden but wasn't beaten far when third over C&D in March; may have had an off-day when beaten 18l at Leicester (7f, good to firm) the following month; sports first-time blinkers and impossible to write off.

runners_data.name: Ritaal
runners_data.note: Patient runner returning from 141-day layoff with new connections but proven course form
runners_data.comment: Didn't get the breaks but still underwhelmed on stable debut latest; new trip/h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up, beaten around 5l, in two Wolverhampton fillies' maidens (7f/6f) in November when trained by Owen Burrows; sold for 28,000gns the following month but two lesser runs for new yard since; wears first-time cheekpieces and has something to prove now.

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: Consistent placer whose hold-up style suits but lacks the finishing kick to win at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Has made the frame six times but remains a maiden; needs to show a shade more in order to bag her first win.

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Course specialist with prominent tendencies but recent form suggests decline from peak
runners_data.comment: Favourably treated on the pick of her turf form and holds an each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: Landed her fourth AW win when scoring over C&D in April; has been beaten three times since at this track, twice on AW, and although she cannot be discounted she is more exposed than the rest of the field.

runners_data.name: Hamaleel
runners_data.note: Natural leader who must survive the anticipated pressure from four prominent runners wanting his position
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who won over 1m here in January; return to 7f may be no bad thing
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to get off the mark at Kempton (1m, AW) in January; has run with credit employing same tactics three times since without managing to sustain her effort; first-time blinkers replace cheekpieces and likely to be the one to catch.

races.paceDynamic: Hamaleel will lead from the gate but faces serious pressure from four prominent runners (Doodling, Polka Blue, Bella Bisbee, Diamondinthedark) who will create a bunched, contested early pace. The inevitable scrimmaging for position among the prominent group will set up a moderate to strong gallop that should suit the hold-up brigade. With five horses wanting to be within two lengths of the lead, the pace will be honest and sustainable rather than suicidal, creating perfect conditions for the closers to pick off tired leaders in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early traffic and finish with one run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalize Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet create sustained pressure on Hamaleel through halfway
scenarios.body: The honest pace will string out the field and leave the front-runners vulnerable to late swoops from horses with one run in them. Sahana and Ritaal benefit most from their patient tactics as the early pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Group Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Hamaleel settles the prominent runners and they travel comfortably to the straight
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more moderate allowing one of the early leaders to sustain their effort to the line. Polka Blue's recent Leicester win and Bella Bisbee's course form make them the most likely beneficiaries of a tactical affair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes too fast early and multiple horses hit the wall
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole with no clear pace bias. Any horse with a turn of foot regardless of position can capitalize on the disjointed finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wire-to-Wire Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Hamaleel gets an uncontested lead and the prominent horses fail to apply pressure
scenarios.body: The leader gets away with soft fractions and has enough left to repel late challenges. Hamaleel's previous front-running success at Kempton gives him the template to repeat the dose.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Hamaleel gets pressured early by multiple prominent runners as he may not sustain his effort like at recent Kempton attempts
Monitor Diamondinthedark for fitness signs given 187-day absence despite her impressive course debut
Check if Polka Blue can translate recent turf Leicester form to this all-weather surface
Observe the pace through the first two furlongs as five horses wanting forward positions could create excessive early speed
Watch for Sahana to be positioned patiently as she needs cover and a strong pace to show her best

runners_data.name: River In Paradise
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000gns yearling; first foal; by Lope Y Fernandez; dam 1m AW winner (RPR 98), half-sister to useful 1m2f-1m4f winner Look Closely, out of 1m 2yo Listed winning half-sister to US 1m/8.5f Grade 3 winner Thewayiam; makes debut and likely to need more time.

runners_data.name: Defiant Dream
runners_data.spotlight: 1,000gns yearling; second foal; by Dream Ahead; dam 7f winner (RPR 70), half-sister to winners Kiniro (6f), Perfect Charm (5f), Inflamed (1m/8.6f 2yo) and Lucio Vero (French 1m6f/15.5f), out of 6f Listed winner; yard's first 2yo runner of the season and likely to need time.

runners_data.name: It'sbeenemotional
runners_data.spotlight: Showed ability when fourth of ten on her debut at Kempton (6f, AW; 9-1) 15 days ago, gradually getting the hang of things as the race developed; should be sharper with that run under her belt.

runners_data.name: Holliesthedollie
runners_data.spotlight: Hung left throughout when beaten 12l on her debut at Bath (5.5f, firm; 20-1) in April; steps up in trip on AW debut and needs to show improvement.

runners_data.name: Fire Thunder
runners_data.comment: Finished well to go close at 25-1 on Wolverhampton debut (6f, AW); respected
runners_data.spotlight: Showed plenty when runner-up in similar events at Wolverhampton and Windsor last month; looks like a winner waiting to happen and must be on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Rocsane
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 13l on debut at Yarmouth (6f, good to soft) last month; makes AW debut and will know more this time.

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny
runners_data.comment: Showed more over 6f at Ripon on her second start; has shown speed; now drops back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 12l when fifth of ten on her debut at Musselburgh (5f, soft) in April but showed more when sixth of eight at Ripon (6f, good) last month; holds place claims.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Jem
runners_data.comment: April 28,000euros foal by Calyx; 14,000gns yearling; yard not noted for winning newcomers
runners_data.spotlight: Always behind when beating only one rival at Windsor (6f, good to firm; 80-1) 12 days ago; AW debut; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Doha Rd
runners_data.comment: Ninth of 13 over C&D on last month's debut, making some late headway; can do better
runners_data.spotlight: Slowly away in two runs at Bath (5f, good); steps up in trip on AW debut and needs to break on terms.

runners_data.name: Crystal Kraken
runners_data.spotlight: Showing steady improvement and was third of 15 at Redcar (6f, good; 100-1) last month on her latest start; needs more in order to win one of these but will be of interest when the nursery season starts.

runners_data.name: Potters Margot
runners_data.note: Debutant with promising Lope Y Fernandez pedigree but inexperienced jockey Jack Callan adds question marks
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; seventh foal; Lope Y Fernandez half-sister to winners Gigi's Beach (6f-1m AW; RPR 70) and Ciyounesse (German 1m/8.5f including AW); dam US 1m turf 2yo winner (including stakes; 100); nice enough pedigree but likely to need a run or two.

runners_data.name: Zigazig Ah
runners_data.note: Rajasinghe filly from Richard Spencer stable that excels with 2yo debutants, Saffie Osborne booking suggests confidence
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; 13,000gns yearling; fourth foal; Rajasinghe sister to winners Giant (7f/1m AW including 2yo; RPR 90) and I Follow Rivers (7f AW; 70); dam Listed-placed 6f/7f winner (including 2yo; 95); yard 2-26 with 2yos on the AW here; market can guide.

runners_data.name: Clear Horizon
runners_data.note: Another debutant with Without Parole breeding suggesting 6f-1m capability, Rob Hornby a positive jockey booking
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; 12,000gns yearling; fourth foal; Without Parole sister to 1m4f winner Emily Rebecca (RPR 67), half-sister to 1m winner Dashing Darcey (including 2yo/AW; 98); dam 7f AW winner (58) from  family of fine sprinters Deacon Blues and The Tin Man; yard's newcomers can go well at a price on debut.

runners_data.name: Deja Vu Diva
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but faded badly when 250-1 at Yarmouth debut, 22 days since last run may help fitness
runners_data.comment: February foal; 2,500gns yearling; half-sister to two winners; yard 0-16 with 2yos
runners_data.spotlight: Bred to be speedy but she achieved little on her Yarmouth debut (6f; 250-1) in May; one to watch for now.

runners_data.name: Ron's Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who impressed when second on Bath debut, Rossa Ryan retains the ride which is encouraging
runners_data.spotlight: Friendless in the market for Bath debut (5f) in May but she travelled strongly and found only one with previous experience too good (the pair clear of the third who has run well since); should cope with this sharp 6f now switched to AW; good claims under Rossa Ryan who's 9-25 for yard in recent years.

runners_data.name: Dun Eideann
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who made late progress into sixth on AW debut 24 days ago, similar going experience is plus
runners_data.spotlight: 25-1 for Wolverhampton AW debut (6f) 24 days ago and although never remotely involved after starting slowly, she did make some late inroads into sixth of 11; should know more this time and can improve.

runners_data.name: Forest Berry
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader who showed class when second at Chepstow recently, Sir Mark Prescott excels with front runners
runners_data.spotlight: Most of her pedigree suggests 1m+ should suit but her dam won at about 6f in the US and this 2yo showed plenty of dash when runner-up at Chepstow (6f) recently on her second start; should improve further on this return to Polytrack; can be involved again.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Sardinia
runners_data.note: Prominent type but fades in finish, tongue-tied again after poor Yarmouth effort 15 days ago
runners_data.comment: 33-1 when last of eight at Newmarket last month; now tried in a tongue tie
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form when failing to beat a rival in 5f events at Newmarket (made the running and faded) and Yarmouth (first time tongue tied); minor handicaps on the agenda after today.

runners_data.name: Happy Humpo
runners_data.note: Prominent early but lacks finishing kick, seller form at Chester suggests limited ability for this grade
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on debut (5f) but bred to do better and well drawn; check betting
runners_data.spotlight: Minor form over 5f at Beverley and when dropped into a seller at Chester (6f; 20-1); has a lot to find in a maiden.

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Hold-up style who showed improvement when fifth at Newmarket, 20 days off may help Stuart Williams charge
runners_data.comment: 66-1 and always out the back when last of ten at Kempton (6f, AW) a fortnight ago
runners_data.spotlight: 66-1 and remote on Kempton AW debut but there was much more evidence of ability when fifth of 13 at Newmarket (6f; 200-1) to a useful winner, looking likely to finish third until two rivals came past very late on; can improve further but handicaps may be her best option.

races.paceDynamic: Forest Berry is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the gates, likely getting an uncontested lead with Ron's Angel and Sea Of Sardinia settling prominently behind her. The modest pace pressure allows Forest Berry to control fractions, while the three debutants (Potters Margot, Zigazig Ah, Clear Horizon) add unknown variables that could disrupt typical positioning. With limited early pace and a small field, this sets up as a tactical affair where those able to travel into contention from mid-race will have the advantage. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close enough to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry gets soft fractions on the front end without serious pace pressure
scenarios.body: Forest Berry's recent Chepstow second shows she has the class edge here, and with no genuine pace rivals she can dictate ideal splits before kicking clear. Her trainer Sir Mark Prescott excels with front runners who get easy leads.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three newcomers (Potters Margot, Zigazig Ah, Clear Horizon) shows significant improvement from their breeding
scenarios.body: The promising pedigrees suggest untapped ability, and debutants often benefit from the tactical nature of small maiden fields. Fresh horses can exploit the modest early pace by positioning perfectly for a late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ron's Angel or Sea Of Sardinia can settle closer to the pace and produce their best form
scenarios.body: Ron's Angel showed real promise when second on debut at Bath, while Sea Of Sardinia has tactical pace to position well behind Forest Berry's lead. The lack of pace pressure allows these types to conserve energy for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the final furlong creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Deja Vu Diva, Dun Eideann and Last Dandelion could benefit from a messy finish where early positioning matters less. However, their previous form suggests they lack the class to capitalize even in ideal circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Forest Berry's early positioning is crucial - if she breaks cleanly and establishes lead without pressure, she becomes very difficult to peg back
Watch the three debutants (Potters Margot, Zigazig Ah, Clear Horizon) in the market on the day as any support suggests stable confidence in their readiness
Ron's Angel needs to settle closer to the pace than her Bath debut where she raced too freely in rear early
Sea Of Sardinia's tendency to fade suggests she needs to be much closer turning for home than in her previous starts
Any non-runners significantly change the pace dynamic as this already relies on Forest Berry as the lone front runner

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner stepping up to one mile after reportedly losing her action on turf debut, needs the tactical setup to favour closers
runners_data.spotlight: Steady improvement on AW during the winter but reportedly lost her action when beaten 12l on turf/handicap debut at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) in April; steps up in trip and needs to get back on track on this return to AW.

runners_data.name: Lordsbridge Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer making first attempt at one mile, his front-running tendencies should suit this tactical setup perfectly
runners_data.comment: Weakened into seventh on his handicap debut at Lingfield; drops back to 7f on turf debut
runners_data.spotlight: Made steady progress in novice/maiden company but hasn't gone on in a couple of handicaps since, on latest start beaten 22l on turf debut here last month; first-time hood needs to being about improvement.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer making AW debut, faces tactical disadvantage with most rivals employing similar late-running styles
runners_data.comment: Ties in with Takeitorleaveit on reappearance running and may build on that effort
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent in her five runs to date; makes AW debut and she needs that bit extra in order to register her first win.

runners_data.name: Ruiz
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but has never finished ahead of a rival in three starts, easy to dismiss on all evidence
runners_data.spotlight: Has yet to finish ahead of a rival in three starts; steps up in trip in handicap debut but easy to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Hove Ranger
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 99-day break, previous AW form over course and distance gives him solid claims despite layoff
runners_data.comment: Found just a subsequent winner too strong on handicap debut; obvious claims off same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Found just a subsequent winner too strong on handicap debut over C&D in January; went one place better at Kempton (7f, AW) the following month; has scope for further improvement following a break and should go close.

runners_data.name: Case Study
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front runner wearing first-time cheekpieces, perfectly positioned to exploit the lack of early pace
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced in four starts, including on handicap debut at Newmarket (1m, good; 28-1) last month; takes a drop in class in first-time cheekpieces and is in good hands, so there could be more to come from her.

runners_data.name: Sail On Sailor
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in excellent form after recent Bath victory, the 3lb penalty may not stop his progression
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on his first two starts for this yard before opening his account at Bath (1m, good) last month, leading in the final strides; more to do off 3lb higher on return to AW but may have more to give.

runners_data.name: Fallacious Promise
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has been knocking on the door, the drop back to one mile could unlock improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Found one too good for the second time in succession up in trip at Newcastle (1m2f, AW; 5-4) last month; knocking on the door and this drop back to 1m could pay dividends.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with fading tendencies, stepping up in trip on handicap debut with apprentice jockey claiming 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Has beaten only three rivals in her three runs over 6f; steps up in trip on handicap debut and more is required from her.

runners_data.name: Laurasia
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 293 days off, hard to fancy given lengthy absence and moderate previous form
runners_data.spotlight: Moderate debut and beaten 21l at 50-1 on her second start, after which she left James Owen for 1,000gns; last of eight last August on first start for this stable and big improvement is required up in trip on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Mist Of Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with fading tendencies returning after 217-day break, needs to find significant improvement on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in three 7f AW runs last autumn; up in trip and needs to pull out more on this handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Case Study is the sole confirmed front runner and will set a comfortable pace from the start with Lordsbridge Bay and Moonlight Angel providing some early support in prominent positions. The moderate early gallop will intensify from halfway as the hold-up horses begin their challenge, creating a sustained finish rather than a sprint. With most of the field employing hold-up tactics and no genuine pace pressure on Case Study early, this race strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can dictate terms and kick clear when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Case Study gets an uncontested lead and maintains his position turning for home.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows him to conserve energy before quickening clear in the straight. His prominent style and first-time cheekpieces give him every chance to convert his tactical advantage into victory.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace becomes a sitting duck scenario for the closers in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks with Sail On Sailor and Fallacious Promise having the class edge. Their recent winning form and ability to quicken late proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Lordsbridge Bay stalks Case Study before challenging approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The step back to one mile suits his racing style better than his recent longer trips and he can outfinish the leader. His prominent running style positions him perfectly to strike when Case Study's effort flattens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Improving Three-Year-Old
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Summer produces her best effort stepping up in trip with steady improvement pattern continuing.
scenarios.body: Despite her hold-up style facing tactical disadvantages, her winter progress on the all-weather surfaces gives her an outside chance. The longer distance allows her more time to wind up her challenge from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Case Study could get an uncontested lead if Lordsbridge Bay and Moonlight Angel fail to go forward early enough to apply pressure
Watch for Sail On Sailor and Fallacious Promise getting squeezed for room in the straight as multiple hold-up horses converge
Hove Ranger returning from 99-day layoff may need this run despite his previous course and distance success
First-time cheekpieces on Case Study could provide the extra focus needed to convert his tactical advantage
Angel Summer stepping up in trip for the first time may find the longer distance exposes her stamina limitations
